answer: Each applicant must fund a sealed vault that pays a small continuous fee and cannot be emptied until three epochs of uniquely graded work have landed. Unlock capacity is rationed by a daily tide quota tied to the vault's age, so one operator cannot drain a herd in a single afternoon. Graders plot answer embeddings against request clocks; names that sit on the same ridge of near-duplicate vectors and synchronized unlocks are treated as one body and slashed together. Cheap keys then burn fees without minting extra votes.
